title: Glucose Appearance and Mitochondrial Biogenesis
proposition: Postprandial glucose-appearance kinetics may influence mitochondrial biogenesis signalling.
rationale: Nutrient availability and metabolic signalling can influence mitochondrial adaptation pathways. Whether the rate of post-meal glucose appearance itself influences this signalling remains a testable question.

contextual.explanation: The training study records muscle mitochondrial-content and regulatory markers, with unchanged total PGC-1alpha. It provides exercise/endpoint context, not a test of glucose-appearance mediation.
contextual.label: SF1 — Interval training increases muscle mitochondrial-content markers

contextual.explanation: Defined fibre studies measured changes in glucose appearance, including a null primary endpoint in one preparation. They did not measure mitochondrial biogenesis; this is measurement context, not direct support or contradiction of the hypothesis.
contextual.label: SF4 — Defined fibre preparations affect appearance differently

evidence_sources.label: Hill et al. (2013) — Carbohydrate and whey protein co-ingestion
evidence_sources.proposition: The carbohydrate–whey exercise study reported altered post-exercise PGC-1alpha mRNA expression.
evidence_sources.limitations: The study did not establish measured glucose-appearance kinetics as the mediator or directly demonstrate mitochondrial formation.

limitations: Measured postprandial glucose appearance was not established as the mediator.
Acute PGC-1alpha transcription is not direct evidence of mitochondrial formation.
No causal dietary-to-brain or ADHD outcome is established.
The linked Findings address different studies and endpoints; their combination does not establish the proposed causal chain.
alternative_explanations: Insulin responses, glycogen availability and total energy availability.
Protein/amino-acid exposure and nutrient composition independent of glucose-appearance rate.
required_evidence: Measure postprandial glucose-appearance kinetics using an appropriate tracer approach and prespecified rate/time-course endpoints.
Link those measured kinetics to mitochondrial-biogenesis signalling and longitudinal mitochondrial-content/formation endpoints, with tissue and assay limitations explicit.
Control or separately assess exercise, insulin, glycogen, protein exposure and energy availability; test mediation rather than equating carbohydrate exposure with glucose appearance.
Replicate in the relevant population; brain or ADHD claims would require their own direct evidence.
